item.title: Life on the move in a changing Chesapeake Bay
item.description: In 2025, a local crabber reached out to professor Romuald Lipcius with some news: He'd been catching stone crabs in the Chesapeake Bay. Native to Florida, the species had reached its northernmost documented occurrence to date. News got out, and William & Mary's VIMS & Batten School were flooded with additional sightings from the public. Some were legitimate; many were mistaken identities. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fire losses to U.S. buildings could nearly triple by 2060 without new protections
item.description: Fires in the U.S. are getting faster, larger and more dangerous, but people continue to develop and move into fire-prone regions. New research from the University of Colorado Boulder's Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences (CIRES) shows that if we don't act on climate change, which fuels fires, manage vegetation or transform how we build and adapt to fire, the risk to structures in the U.S. will almost triple by midcentury. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Reservoir, human activity impact Ravi River's surface water availability by fivefold
item.description: What does a healthy river look like? For most of us, an obvious answer would involve two aspects: water flowing through a channel and green vegetation along its banks. However, in reality, a river's health depends on several factors, such as how much water flows through it, how water moves through the landscape, how that flow changes with the seasons, how sediment moves downstream, how often it spills into its floodplain and how these processes change with the seasons. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hay quien propone hacer el mantenimiento del turbo de tu coche cada 10.000 kilómetros pero la realidad es más compleja
item.description: "El 98% de los coches llevan turbo". Es la declaración de Miquel, mecánico, recogida por los compañeros Motorpasión para explicar por qué debemos tener cuidado con este componente. Dice Homer Simpson que "la gente se inventa estadísticas con tal de demostrar algo y eso lo sabe el 14% de la gente". Pero más allá de que ese 98% sea una estimación más o menos precisa, lo cierto es que la inmensa mayoría de los coches que salen al mercado sí llevan turbo. Esto se debe a que los fabricantes se han visto obligados a reducir cilindrada y tamaño del motor para reducir emisiones contaminantes pero, al… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Beavers set to return to Loch Ness after 500 years, with 15 family groups approved for release.
item.description: In an exciting development, wild beavers are about to return to Loch Ness after centuries of absence. The Scottish nature agency NatureScot has sanctioned their release as part of a transformative rewilding project. Over the next three years, conservationists will introduce family groups of beavers to the area’s waterways, focusing on enhancing biodiversity and wildlife habitats, while also implementing strategies to resolve any conflicts with local farmers and landowners. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Colorado community fights plan to use drones to spray weed killer
item.description: Officials in Boulder County, Colorado, say they have a safe plan to wipe out invasive weeds, but some locals are concerned Soon, weed-killing chemicals will start falling from the sky over the Red Hill area of Boulder county, Colorado. The wildland is known for its biodiversity , home to hundreds of important species and a concentration of rare environmental resources. It is a key habitat for beloved herds of elk and bighorn sheep, with farms and ranchland lying at its base. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Hemos llenado las ciudades de árboles para combatir el calor. Un nuevo estudio advierte que a veces pueden lograr exactamente lo contrario
item.description: Durante los últimos años hemos escuchado de manera reiterada que plantar árboles era una de las soluciones para combatir el cambio climático y el aumento de las temperaturas en los entornos urbanos. Algo que es bastante necesario, puesto que los datos apuntan a que en 93 ciudades europeas, el 4,33% de las muertes durante el verano de 2015 se atribuyeron al efecto isla de calor. De esta manera, llevar la cobertura arbórea de nuestras ciudades al 30 % enfriaría la temperatura media unos 0,4 °C y evitaría más de 2.600 muertes prematuras. No es tan fácil. Aunque parece que lo correcto es comenzar… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: COP17: Los países acuerdan una hoja de ruta para acelerar la protección de la biodiversidad
item.description: La cumbre de biodiversidad de la ONU concluyó en Armenia con una hoja de ruta para acelerar el cumplimiento de los objetivos mundiales de protección de la naturaleza antes de 2030. Los países anunciaron cerca de 2000 millones de dólares en nueva financiación y acordaron reforzar la participación de los pueblos indígenas en las decisiones internacionales. Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: The Great Barrier Reef's most notorious coral killer may actually be helping it
item.description: Crown-of-thorns starfish are notorious for devouring coral reefs, but surprising new research reveals these spiny predators may actually help reefs thrive when their populations are kept in check. Scientists studying Australia's Great Barrier Reef discovered that nearly 75% of observed starfish feeding events left behind living coral tissue, rather than destroying entire colonies. By feeding on fast-growing, dominant corals, the starfish create opportunities for slower-growing species to survive, potentially increasing coral biodiversity. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: US river straightened 110 years ago to drain land, now set for restoration to reduce floods
item.description: Authorities in Tennessee, US, have acquired 985 acres along the South Fork of the Forked Deer River to reduce flooding and restore natural habitats. The river was straightened in 1916 to drain surrounding land, but the changes contributed to flash floods and erosion. The restoration project aims to reconnect the river with its floodplain and eventually open the area to the public. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Environmental Defense Fund analysis shows administration handed out $950m and Clean Air Act exemptions It’s a good time to be a coal plant in the US. item.title: Cambio climático: Nueva York se protege elevando un parque para contener la subida del nivel del mar
item.description: Catorce años después del huracán Sandy, Nueva York eleva hasta tres metros el East River Park y construye muros y compuertas ocultas para proteger a más de 110.000 residentes, con una inversión de 2000 millones de dólares. La ONU advierte de que 770 millones de personas viven a menos de cinco metros sobre la pleamar y pide "más financiación predecible" para la adaptación al cambio climático. Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: Healey to veto new offshore wind projects if they will not lower bills
item.description: UK chancellor’s plans add to concerns government is moving away from pro-renewables agenda John Healey has said he will veto new offshore wind projects if they will not lower bills, adding to concerns that the government is moving away from the pro-renewables agenda. Announcing his plans, the chancellor said clean power is “how we break the grip of international gas prices on our bills”, but added the shift towards it “has to come at the right pace, in the right places, with the grid to carry it”.
